request:POST /v1/groups/{groupId}/node-a.description:
Two authentication methods are supported (mutually exclusive - exactly one must be used):

**Method 1: challenge_response** - Traditional signature verification.
Requires `challenge_response` and `node_id`. Works for both Matter and non-Matter groups.
The node is immediately added to the group. No NOC is generated.

**Method 2: nocsr_elements** - Matter attestation with NOC generation.
Requires `nocsr_elements`, `attestation_challenge`, and `attestation_signature`.
Only valid for Matter-capable groups. Returns a device NOC. Call /confirm after
the device installs the NOC.

challenge_response.description:
Hex-encoded signature of the SHA256 hash of the challenge, signed by the node's private key.
**Mutually exclusive with nocsr_elements** - exactly one must be provided.

node_id.description:
The ID of the node to be associated.
**Required when using challenge_response.**
**Optional/ignored when using nocsr_elements** - the node_id is extracted from
vendor_reserved1 or auto-generated for pure Matter nodes (16-character hex string, 8 bytes).

nocsr_elements.description:
Hex-encoded NOCSRElements TLV structure for Matter attestation verification.
**Only valid for Matter-capable groups.**
**Mutually exclusive with challenge_response** - exactly one must be provided.

Contains CSR (extracted for NOC generation), CSRNonce, and optional vendor_reserved
fields. The CSRNonce must match the challenge from the /initiate step.

If vendor_reserved1 contains a nodeID (thing name), the attestation signature
will be verified against registered certificates for that node. If no certificates
are found, or if vendor_reserved1 is not present, the device is treated as a
pure Matter node and a random 16-character hex node_id (8 bytes) is generated.

The TLV structure format:
- Tag 0x01: CSR (DER-encoded Certificate Signing Request)
- Tag 0x02: CSRNonce (must match the 32-byte challenge from /initiate)
- Tag 0x03: vendor_reserved1 (optional, contains nodeID/thing name)
- Tag 0x04: vendor_reserved2 (optional)
- Tag 0x05: vendor_reserved3 (optional)

attestation_challenge.description:
Hex-encoded 16-byte attestation challenge from PASE/CASE session.
**Required when nocsr_elements is provided.**
Used together with NOCSRElements to compute the TBS (to-be-signed):
SHA256(NOCSRElements || AttestationChallenge).

attestation_signature.description:
Hex-encoded 64-byte ECDSA signature in raw r||s format (32 bytes r, 32 bytes s).
This is the signature over SHA256(NOCSRElements || AttestationChallenge).
**Required when nocsr_elements is provided.**

For devices with registered certificates (nodeID found in vendor_reserved1),
this signature is verified against the device's DAC public key.
For pure Matter devices (no vendor_reserved1 or no certificates), signature
verification is skipped.

request:PUT /v1/groups/{groupId}/nodes/{.description:
The schedule service payload. Follows the ESP RainMaker built-in
Schedules specification — this is the exact structure the device
parses. The cloud stores and forwards it unchanged.

items.description:
A single schedule entry. The firmware uses `name` as an NVS key and
requires it to be 16 characters or fewer. Additional keys (including
`id`) are ignored by the device but stored by the cloud.

id.description: Cloud-side identifier. Opaque; the device ignores this field.

name.description: Unique schedule name (also used as an NVS key on the device).

triggers.description: One or more triggers that fire the schedule.

items.description:
Schedule trigger. The trigger kind is discriminated by which keys are
present — there is no explicit `type` field:

- **One-shot relative:** `rsec` (seconds after current time).
- **Date-based:** `m` (minutes since midnight) plus at least one of
  `d` (day-of-week bitmask) / `dd` (day-of-month).
- **Solar:** `lat` + `lon` plus exactly one of `sr` / `ss` (offset in
  minutes from sunrise/sunset). May also include `d`/`dd`/`mm`/`yy`.

rsec.description: Seconds after current time (one-shot relative trigger).

d.description:
Bitmask of days of week (bits 7..1 = Sun/Sat/.../Tue/Mon).
Example: `5` (0b0000101) = Mon + Wed.

mm.description:
Bitmask of months (bits 12..1 = Dec/Nov/.../Feb/Jan).
Example: `15` (0b000000001111) = Jan–Apr.

sr.description: Offset in minutes from sunrise (solar trigger).

ss.description: Offset in minutes from sunset (solar trigger).

action.description:
Node parameter-update payload applied when the schedule fires.
Default data model: `{ <DeviceId>: { <ParamId>: <value>, ... }, ... }`.
Matter data model: parameter-control payload
`{ "0x<endpoint>": { "c": { "s": { "0x<cluster>": { "c": { "0x<command>": "<TLV hex>" } } } } } }`.

validity.description: Optional validity window for the schedule.

start.description: Start of validity window, UNIX timestamp in seconds.

end.description: End of validity window, UNIX timestamp in seconds.
